raw_record.support_text: In their systematic review, Bernardo et al. (2016) concluded that there was no association between aspartame consumption and increased risk of cancers of the brain, or of the hematopoietic, digestive, and reproductive systems.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: adult and child consumers in the systematic review by Bernardo et al. (2016)
raw_record.extra_details: Negative association finding from a systematic review of cancer studies.

raw_record.support_text: Labutina et al. 2013 reported for bone cancer in Mayak workers: no definite dose response, with only 4 cases involving plutonium exposure.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: No definite dose response observed; only 4 cases with plutonium exposure limit the analysis.
raw_record.extra_details: Dosimetry version 2008; cohort study with smoking adjustment.

raw_record.support_text: In a 2-year feeding study in mice, the incidence and types of neoplastic lesions observed in hexazinone-treated mice were similar to those seen in the controls (common to the strain employed), and it was concluded that the chemical is not tumorigenic in the mouse. The no-effect level was 200 ppm.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: 2-year feeding study in mice; no-effect level 200 ppm
raw_record.extra_details: Neoplastic lesion incidence and types in treated mice were similar to those in controls and common to the strain employed.

raw_record.support_text: In a large series of hyperthyroid patients followed up for nearly a lifetime, cancer mortality was not significantly elevated. raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: hyperthyroid patients followed for nearly a lifetime

raw_record.support_text: The urinary bladder tumor effect seen in ad libitum fed male rats was not seen using the dietary restriction protocol; no urinary bladder tumors were seen in the restricted controls or the restricted 1X group at two or three years.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Male rats; feed-restriction (dietary restriction) protocol; no bladder tumors in restricted controls or restricted 1X group at two or three years.

raw_record.support_text: 6-week-old C57BL/6 mice treated with 500 µg/mL arecoline for 28 weeks developed no oral lesions or tumors; separately, oral administration of arecoline (1000 µg/mL) through drinking water for 20 weeks produced no pathological changes in the oral mucosa.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Dose 500 µg/mL for 28 weeks (C57BL/6) and 1000 µg/mL via drinking water for 20 weeks; negative only for oral neoplasia/pathology in mice.
raw_record.extra_details: Merges two mouse studies: Kuo et al. (500 µg/mL, 28 weeks, no oral lesions or tumors) and Wen et al. [25] (1000 µg/mL drinking water, 20 weeks, no oral mucosal pathological changes).

raw_record.support_text: There was neither macroscopic nor microscopic evidence of tumor in any rabbit in which the bladder was studied. In the discussion it is stated that no tumors developed in the rabbits during the 12-month period, indicating rats are more sensitive than rabbits to methylcholanthrene.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Bladder studies in rabbits; observation period of 12 months. No tumor by macroscopic or microscopic examination.
raw_record.extra_details: Rats were reported more sensitive to methylcholanthrene than rabbits; a longer period (3 to 5 years) is thought to be needed to form experimental neoplasms in rabbits.

raw_record.support_text: No colonic tumors or dysplastic lesions were found after exposure to either the CMNC N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea alone or DSS alone in male CD2F1 mice given 4% DSS in drinking water for 1 week.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Agent administered alone without DSS co-treatment; reflects the agent's designation as a colon-mutagenic non-carcinogen with no colonic tumorigenic effect on its own.
raw_record.extra_details: The agent is described as a colon-mutagenic non-carcinogen (CMNC) that is not a colon carcinogen by itself.

raw_record.support_text: Oral administration of 4,4'-methylene-bis-(2-chloroaniline) to mice and rats induced lung tumors in rats [6, 9, 12, 15, 16].

raw_record.extra_details: In the DPN study it reduced the hepatocarcinogenic action of DPN.

raw_record.support_text: The paper refers to 'hepatic tumors elicited in trout by ... 7,12-dimethylbenzanthracene (DMBA) (Fong et al., 1993)' that carry carcinogen-specific Ki-ras oncogenic mutations, indicating DMBA elicited hepatic tumors in trout.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA = 7,12-dimethylbenzanthracene; elicited tumors carried carcinogen-specific Ki-ras oncogenic mutations; cited from Fong et al., 1993.

raw_record.support_text: Injection of carcinogens such as dimethylhydrazine (DMH) or azoxymethane (AOM) into rats induces intestinal cancers that can be modified by diet, whereas in pigs DMH produces hepatic necrosis without any intestinal tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: Used as a diet-modifiable experimental rodent colon-cancer model; DMH (dimethylhydrazine).

raw_record.support_text: In long-term drinking water studies, significant dose-related increases in tumors of the kidney were seen in rats treated with 1,3-dichloro-2-propanol.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Significant dose-related increases observed in long-term drinking water studies in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: No information available on 1,3-dichloro-2-propanol carcinogenicity in mice.

raw_record.support_text: Methylcholanthrene (MCA) interacts with DNA resulting in somatic mutation which confers a growth advantage on the target cell and results in clonal proliferation of tumor cells, which may contain highly immunogenic tumor-specific-transplant antigens (TSTA). The paper reports a highly immunogenic methylcholanthrene (MCA)-induced fibrosarcoma used to immunize C57/BL female mice, indicating that MCA induces fibrosarcoma tumors in intact mice.
raw_record.extra_details: MCA is described as interacting with DNA causing somatic mutation, clonal proliferation of tumor cells, and production of immunogenic tumor-specific-transplant antigens (TSTA); the induced fibrosarcoma was used to immunize C57/BL female mice.

raw_record.support_text: In a rat carcinogenicity bioassay, dose-related significant increases were seen in mammary gland adenomas in female bemitradine-treated animals.
raw_record.extra_details: Mammary neoplasms often caused death in treated females; palpable masses appeared sooner and at greater incidence in females.

raw_record.support_text: Neoplasia induced in man by radionuclides is benchmarked by studies of dial painters, radium chemists, and patients receiving radium as a therapeutic nostrum. The important nuclides are 226Ra (half-life 1620 yr), 228Ra (Mesothorium, half-life 5.7 yr) and their decay products.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: human dial painters, radium chemists, and patients receiving radium therapy (over 800 studied from a known population of over 2200)
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: bone tumors, including sarcomas and head carcinomas
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Radiogenic tumors seen at cumulative skeletal doses above about 1000-1200 rads, with no clinically significant change below a residual body burden of about 0.5 uCi of pure 226Ra; incidence stayed nearly constant over 1000-20,000 cumulative rads.
raw_record.extra_details: Mean bone tumor occurrence among epidemiologically suitable (unselected) high-dose cases was 0.28 +/- 0.06; no linear analytical function fits the dose-response relationship for tumor incidence; a dose-rate effect was suggested in contrast to animal alpha-emitter experiments. Related nuclides 228Ra (Mesothorium) and decay products are also implicated.
